The API spells names without diacritics. The 2022 census names page returned HTTP 403, so no surname list was taken. Files used: 1930M, 1930F, 1940M, 1940F, 1950M, 1950F, 1960M, 1960F, 1970M, 1970F, 1980M, 1980F, 1990M, 1990F, 2000M, 2000F, 2010M, 2010F. Weights are estimates of relative commonness inside this list: the most frequent kept name is 100 and the rest are rounded in proportion. They are not shares of all births and they are not comparable across lists.

There is no official German given-name statistic. These lists are the Gesellschaft für deutsche Sprache top tens published on one page, scored as 11 minus rank and summed across the years of the band. That is a rank score, not a birth count. Where a cell groups spellings with a slash, only the first spelling is kept. A parenthetical optional letter such as '(h)' was removed. For 1994–1996 the page splits the old and new federal states; a name keeps its better rank that year. Years present: 1977–2025. Nothing before 1977 is on the page. The longer top-200 lists are sold, not published here. No German surname frequency table was opened.

Given names are Insee birth counts for France (Mayotte only from 2012), with annual counts rounded by Insee to the nearest multiple of five. The file covers 1920–2025. Surnames are the Insee national file of names given at least 30 times to people born in France from 1891 to 2000. Decade columns do not match these bands exactly: 1920–1949 uses 1921–1930, 1931–1940 and 1941–1950; 1950–1979 uses 1951–1960, 1961–1970 and 1971–1980; 1980–2009 uses 1981–1990 and 1991–2000. The 2010–2039 surname list repeats 1991–2000 because the file stops at births in 2000. The surname file spells names without accents. All-capital source spellings were title-cased. Weights are estimates of relative commonness inside this list: the most frequent kept name is 100 and the rest are rounded in proportion. They are not shares of all births and they are not comparable across lists.

England and Wales only; Scotland and Northern Ireland are not in these files. For 1920–1949 the given-name weights sum (101 minus rank) across the ONS top-100 snapshots for 1924, 1934 and 1944. For 1950–1979 the snapshots are 1954, 1964 and 1974. Those weights are rank scores, not birth counts. Surnames are the top 20 birth surnames in England and Wales in 2014 and 2024 (the two years in the ONS freedom-of-information table), summed where the name appears in both years. The same short list is reused in every band. It is below the 40-name target. A request for a longer resident-population surname list was opened and did not contain one. Weights are estimates of relative commonness inside this list: the most frequent kept name is 100 and the rest are rounded in proportion. They are not shares of all births and they are not comparable across lists.

England and Wales only. Given names for 1980–2009 sum ONS birth counts for 1996–2009. The 1984 and 1994 top-100 snapshots have no counts, so each ranked name also adds an estimated count of round(C × (101 − rank) / 100), where C is the count of the most common name of that sex in 1996. That scale is only there so the two rank lists are not dropped. Surnames are a separate limitation. Surnames are the top 20 birth surnames in England and Wales in 2014 and 2024 (the two years in the ONS freedom-of-information table), summed where the name appears in both years. The same short list is reused in every band. It is below the 40-name target. A request for a longer resident-population surname list was opened and did not contain one. Weights are estimates of relative commonness inside this list: the most frequent kept name is 100 and the rest are rounded in proportion. They are not shares of all births and they are not comparable across lists.

Given names sum first-name registrations in Poland for 2000–2025. The 2000–2019 workbook is one file; 2020–2025 are the separate male and female first-name workbooks. Bands before 2000 have no given names from these files. The 2010–2039 band stops at 2025. Surnames are the masculine PESEL file of living people on 22 January 2025. The same slice is reused in every band. The separate feminine surname file was not merged, so adjectival surnames appear in the masculine citation form only. Weights are estimates of relative commonness inside this list: the most frequent kept name is 100 and the rest are rounded in proportion. They are not shares of all births and they are not comparable across lists.

Counts under five in a year are absent from the file. Surnames are the 2010 Census frequency table for people enumerated that year, not a birth cohort, and the same top slice is reused in every band. Census spellings in the file have no diacritics; all-capital surnames were title-cased. Weights are estimates of relative commonness inside this list: the most frequent kept name is 100 and the rest are rounded in proportion. They are not shares of all births and they are not comparable across lists.
